transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A warm fridge with a still-cold freezer is a classic symptom of an airflow problem. In most frost-free models, there is one cooling coil in the freezer that chills both sections; if the cold air can't get from the freezer into the fridge, the fridge warms up while the freezer stays fine. The simplest and most common cause for this is that the vents allowing cold air to flow are blocked by food or over-packing. Please check inside your fridge compartment (usually at the back wall) for any vents. Are they clear of food items and not obstructed by tightly packed shelves? If you've recently restocked, please move items away from the back panel to ensure free airflow. Let me know if this was the issue or if the vents were already clear.
I can't see any vents in the fridge part, just shelves and a dial at the back. Nothing is packed against the back wall though. Should I really unplug it? The freezer is still holding at about -16C.

Yes, unplugging it for a full manual defrost is the safest and most effective way to check this. It isolates the appliance completely and allows any hidden frost to melt so we can see if that was the problem. In a frost-free fridge, if the defrost heater or thermostat fails, ice builds up on the evaporator coils (usually behind the back panel in the freezer). This ice eventually blocks the airflow into the fridge section, causing exactly what you're seeing. 1. Switch off and unplug the appliance.
2. Remove all food and store it in cool bags or a neighbour's fridge if possible.
3. Leave both doors open for 24 hours to ensure all ice melts completely (place towels down).
4. After 24 hours, check behind the freezer's rear panel. Is there a solid block of ice on the coils, or is it fairly clear? Let me know what you find inside the freezer after this process.

I haven't tried the defrost yet, I'd have to empty everything out first. Also I can't get to any rear panel as it's screwed into the cabinet (landlord's). There's a bit of frost on the freezer back wall, not loads. No burning smell or tripping either. Is there anything easier I can try first?

I understand you don't want to empty the fridge and access the back panel right now. That's fair. In these models, if that system fails, ice builds up behind the back panel where you can't see it. This blocks the cold air from reaching the fridge section. 1. Stand near the freezer compartment (the part that is still -16C).
2. Listen carefully when the compressor kicks in or while it is running.
3. Is there a faint humming or buzzing sound coming from inside the back of the freezer? Or is it completely silent? Please let me know what you hear. If it's silent, the fan might be stuck (also part of the defrost system). If it sounds normal but the fridge stays warm, we are probably looking at a heater or thermostat failure that will need an engineer to replace.
I can hear it running quite a lot, so it's not silent. I can't tell if it's coming from the back of the freezer though. No odd smell.

This points strongly to the automatic defrost system failing. In these models, if the heater or thermostat doesn't work, ice builds up on the coils inside the freezer wall. This blocks the cold air from reaching the fridge section. Because you cannot access the back panel and don't want to empty the appliance for a full 24-hour defrost right now, we have limited options. However, there is one simple check: please look at the bottom of the freezer compartment (inside) for a small drain hole. Is it blocked with ice or debris? If this drain is blocked, water from normal defrosting can't escape and may contribute to freezing issues. If the drain is clear, or if clearing it doesn't solve the problem within 24 hours, you will likely need an engineer to check a part (usually the heater or thermostat) that requires accessing the back panel. Given your rental situation, I would suggest reporting this to your landlord as a repair issue.

I can't see a drain hole in the freezer, but I'm not sure what I'm looking for. If it needs an engineer I'll report it to the letting agent, the landlord says faults go through them. Is there anything else I can check myself?

Given that you cannot access the internal panels and have already ruled out blocked vents and a silent fan, the most likely cause is a fault in the automatic defrost system. This prevents the freezer from melting its normal frost build-up, leading to ice blocking the airflow into the fridge section. Since you are renting and cannot dismantle the unit yourself, there is no further owner-safe check that will fix this. The appliance needs a qualified engineer to replace the faulty component (usually the heater or thermostat) behind the internal panel. Please report this to your letting agent as a repair issue. In the meantime, keep the fridge door closed as much as possible to maintain the temperature in the fridge section for as long as you can, and monitor the freezer temperature to ensure food remains safe.

Defrost system failure causing ice blockage of airflow (medium)
